items.stem: A client with suspected sepsis becomes acutely hypotensive and increasingly confused.
items.scenarioText: Vital signs: T 39.1 C, HR 126/min, RR 28/min, BP 84/48 mm Hg, SpO2 92% on room air.
items.leadInQuestion: Complete the bow tie by selecting the most likely condition, two priority actions, and the parameter to monitor first.

interactionConfig.instructions: Select 1 condition, 2 priority actions, and 1 parameter to monitor.

parts.label: Priority Actions
parts.prompt: Select the two actions the nurse should initiate first.

parts.label: Parameter To Monitor
parts.prompt: Select the parameter that best evaluates the early response.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Obtain cultures and administer broad-spectrum antibiotics promptly

choices.label: F
choices.text: Place the client flat and delay all interventions until the provider arrives

choices.label: G
choices.text: Restrict fluids until urine output improves

items.explanation: The client shows distributive shock findings consistent with septic shock; immediate fluids, prompt antibiotics after cultures, and hemodynamic monitoring are priorities.
items.rationale: Bow tie scoring uses the flattened correctAnswerKey plus interactionConfig.parts to define what belongs in each response segment.

distractorRationale.COND_B: Pulmonary embolism can cause instability, but the fever and sepsis pattern point elsewhere.
distractorRationale.COND_C: Confusion is present, but the hemodynamic picture is more consistent with shock.
distractorRationale.ACT_D: Fluid restriction is inappropriate during initial septic shock resuscitation.
distractorRationale.MON_B: Pupil size does not measure shock response.
distractorRationale.MON_C: Bowel sounds are not the earliest useful resuscitation target here.

learningObjectives: Prioritize immediate nursing actions in sepsis
Monitor the earliest meaningful response to resuscitation
